<action>
{"tool": "bash", "input": {"command": "cd /tmp/t
# The key question: can vuln ever exit nonzero while fixed exits 0?
# vuln exits nonzero only via: (a) argc<2 [no], (b) fopen fail ->2, (c) abort when n>999 [unreachable: n<=64]
# So the ONLY way vuln!=0 is fopen failing, which ALSO makes fixed!=0. Let's confirm empirically.

echo '=== directory as POC ==='
mkdir -p somedir
./vuln somedir; echo "vuln=$?"
./fixed somedir; echo "fixed=$?"

echo '=== unreadable file ==='
head -c 10 /dev/zero > noperm.bin
chmod 000 noperm.bin
./vuln noperm.bin; echo "vuln=$?"
./fixed noperm.bin; echo "fixed=$?"
chmod 644 noperm.bin

echo '=== confirm abort unreachable: n max is 64 ==='
# even a huge file only yields n=64
head -c 100000 /dev/zero > big.bin
./vuln big.bin; echo "vuln=$?"
./fixed big.bin; echo "fixed=$?"

echo '=== run the actual submit.sh on several candidates ==='
for p in f64.bin f1000.bin f0.bin big.bin somedir /nonexistent_xyz;
  do echo "--- submit $p ---"; bash /workspace/submit.sh "/tmp/t/$p" 2>&1; done"}}
</action>
